title: Capstone
tagline: Assemble everything you built into one shareable AI PM portfolio piece.
intro: Nothing new to learn this week — just assembly. You've built a scorecard, a prompt template, a guardrail file, a prototype brief, and a review rubric, all for the I-9 Completion Assistant. That's not a coincidence: it's meant to read as one coherent piece of AI PM work when you put it side by side.

scenario.context: This section pulls together what you built in Weeks 1 through 5, automatically, from what's saved in your browser.
scenario.brief: Five separate exercises don't obviously add up to anything. One document that walks a single feature — the I-9 Completion Assistant — from idea, through spec, through guardrails, through prototype, through review rubric, reads as exactly what an AI PM does day to day. Add a short closing reflection, then export the full portfolio piece as one Markdown file.

sections.heading: Closing reflection
sections.learning: The fastest way to make this stick is to run the same five steps on one real (non-sensitive, or fully within Gemini) feature idea in the next two weeks, before the habit fades — whether that's another I-9 & Onboarding feature, or a different Employer Services line like WOTC screening, offboarding, ACA reporting, unemployment cost management, or ID Watchdog.

example.text: Writing the guardrail file before handing anything to an agent is the habit I'm most likely to keep — I've been skipping straight from idea to ticket, and this gives engineering something concrete to build against. I want to try it next on our ACA reporting assistant, where a bad auto-filed form is a much bigger deal than a bad I-9 flag.

field.label: Your turn: Closing reflection
field.help: In a few sentences: what's the one habit from these five weeks you're most likely to actually use on real work next month, and where would you try it first?
field.placeholder: Name the habit, and the real feature or product line you'd try it on.
